Over one-third, or 36%, of the Form 6 applications accepted for inclusion in Karnataka’s final electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were filed by young or first-time voters aged 18 and 19.
This means that only 4.48 lakh of the 1.07 crore people excluded at the draft stage got back on the rolls, as a significant share of the additions came from new voters.
Between June 16, when the rolls were frozen, and September 23, the last day to file claims and objections, the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) received 7,87,534 Form 6 applications. Of these, 76,176 were rejected and 7,08,110 were accepted.
Of the total accepted applications, 2,59,838 were filed by voters aged 18 and 19, data from the CEO’s office confirmed.
The net additions during the claims and objections period were very low in comparison with the deletions. Of the 1.07 crore names deleted at the draft stage, only 4.48 lakh people were restored to the rolls, while 99.32 lakh names remained deleted in the final list. This suggests that even after including first-time voters, only about seven names were added through Form 6 for every 100 voters deleted at the draft stage.
While a proportion of the deletions could be attributed to redundancies in the rolls – such as 7.09 lakh duplicate entries and 16.39 lakh deceased voters – the remaining and also the largest share of deletions (more than 84.46 lakh) came under the absent and shifted categories. These were people whose names were deleted because they could not be found at their addresses during enumeration or had shifted residence. However, only 4.48 lakh of those deleted at the draft stage managed to get back on the rolls, as rest of the net additions accounted for those filed by new electors.
Bengaluru, which saw the most number of deletions, had its electorate shrink from 1.03 crore before the revision to just 59.08 lakh in the final rolls. During the claims and objections period, the city saw a net addition of 2.74 lakh names. Of these, 41,141 (16.66%) were new voters aged 18 and 19. More than 43 lakh people who were disenfranchised during the draft stage continued to remain off the final rolls.
Kalaburagi, which saw the second-highest number of deletions after Bengaluru, had over 23.71 lakh electors before the SIR began. At the draft stage, over 5.21 lakh names were deleted, accounting for 22% of its electorate and leaving 18,49,585 electors on the rolls.
The final rolls had 18,94,144 electors, a net addition of just 44,559 from the draft stage. Of these, 12,985 were new voters aged 18 and 19, accounting for 29.12% of the additions. The remaining 31,574 were people seeking to get back on the rolls after being excluded under the Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate category.
More than 4.77 lakh names deleted at the draft stage remained excluded.
